explain.say: Eagles hunt from high in the sky, so they need to spot small prey from far away. Their eyes are about as big as ours, even though an eagle's head is much smaller.

faq.q: Why are eagle eyes so sharp?
faq.a: Their eyes are large, and the fovea, the sharpest spot of the retina, is deep and packed with far more cone cells than ours. More cells per patch of image means more detail, like more pixels on a screen.
asks: What makes an eagle's vision sharp?

faq.q: Do eagles see better than humans?
faq.a: For fine detail at a distance, yes: about twice as sharp. Eagles also have two foveae per eye. But humans see better in some ways, and at night both see poorly compared with owls.
asks: How does an eagle eye compare to ours?

faq.q: How far can an eagle see?
faq.a: An eagle can spot something rabbit-sized from roughly 3 kilometres away, where to us it would be a tiny speck. Its sharp vision lets it hunt from high above.
asks: Can an eagle see a rabbit from a mile away?
How far away can a hawk see prey?

faq.q: Why does an eagle have two foveae?
faq.a: One fovea looks sideways and is very sharp for scanning the ground. The other looks forward, letting both eyes work together to judge distance as the eagle dives at prey.
asks: What is the second fovea for?
How do eagles judge distance in a dive?

faq.q: Why do eagles have a bony ridge over their eyes?
faq.a: The brow ridge above an eagle's eye shades it from the sun, like a cap peak, and may protect the eye. It also gives eagles their fierce look.
asks: What is the ridge above an eagle's eye?

facts: Eagles have two foveae in each eye, while humans have one.
Measured visual acuity of the wedge-tailed eagle is roughly twice that of humans.
